task.title: Dry-run the existing Sep 23 Strength reassessment

result.summary: The Founder-authorized Sep 23 reassessment dry-run ran under production runtime 98f8ccec in REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY and safely refused. Exact outcome: refused / single_session_below_confident_threshold; matcher v4 found exactly one candidate with outcome possible_match, confidence 50, basis logger_session_window, startAligned false, endAligned false, overlapSeconds 3826. It proved exactly one same-day canonical Strength workout and exactly one same-day native live Logger Strength session. Root cause: the existing canonical Logger object's captured_at is the server's synthetic noon fallback, not the 14:56 commit instant; its inferred end is therefore 10,632 seconds before the HealthKit end. The stored Native Build 54 record has no finishedAt. Exact predicted mutation: none, because the confident-match gate did not pass. No reassessment, link, assessment update, audit row, policy change, or TestFlight upload occurred.

tests.summary: The deployed candidate retained its reviewed local validation. The production dry-run exposed a missing real-data fixture: tests supplied capturedAt as the actual commit instant, while the existing Native command omitted capturedAt and the Server stored its noon fallback.

review.summary: The earlier source review is still valid for the implemented contracts, but the production dry-run found that the assumed legacy commit-time fallback is not present in the canonical payload. A corrected legacy timestamp source requires a new implementation, mutation proof, and fresh review before any new deploy request.

zero_write_audit.summary: The reassessment entry verified runtime SHA, owner scope, BEGIN REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY, transaction_read_only=on, and rolled back. It used mode=dry-run with no authorization reference. The operation returned refused before constructing or executing mutations. Pre/post deployment audits had already proven all policy, HealthKit, Logger-count, link/claim, strategic, and migration digests unchanged.

decisions_required: Do not authorize reassessment apply: the current production dry-run predicts no mutation and refuses safely.

A new reviewed Server correction must source the legacy Sep 23 Logger commit time from durable storage metadata rather than the synthetic payload captured_at fallback; deploying that future SHA will require separate Founder authorization.
Build 55 TestFlight upload remains a separate approval gate and has not occurred.
blockers: The existing Sep 23 Logger canonical payload has no finishedAt and its captured_at is the Server's noon fallback, so the reviewed matcher cannot prove Logger-end alignment and cannot produce a confident reassessment candidate.
unexpected_findings: The dedicated matcher rule did activate: unique same-day workout/session and basis logger_session_window are proven. The failure is specifically end-time evidence, not ambiguity, wrong session selection, or old code running.

The test fixture modeled capturedAt as the real 14:56 commit instant, but the Native command did not send capturedAt and the Server fell back to local-date noon. That assumption gap escaped the source tests and fresh review.
backlog: Implement the smallest fail-closed legacy reassessment correction using a durable Server-owned commit timestamp, without mutating Logger detail or changing normal future Build 55 finishedAt behavior.
Add a production-shaped regression fixture where payload captured_at is noon fallback and durable record metadata contains the true commit instant; mutation-test and fresh-review the correction.
Request separate authorization for any new Server deploy, then rerun only the Sep 23 read-only dry-run before requesting reassessment apply.
Do not upload Build 55 without separate authorization and do not begin Cardio before Strength reaches its final verdict.
recommended_next_step: Prepare and fresh-review a narrow Server correction that exposes the durable commit timestamp to this one legacy reassessment path. Do not apply the current reassessment; it correctly refused and predicted no writes.
